<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **82** documentable anchor(s).

**21** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f506b79d85790a8f74a762ac4031090c7fbdae25`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f506b79d85790a8f74a762ac4031090c7fbdae25` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1bcbb13d7278e37b8f048d5381f01c837b5a5b85` — the merge of head `c22645ebea8b55d8c6e6592c8546d731657720cb` into base `f506b79d85790a8f74a762ac4031090c7fbdae25`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1bcbb13d7278e37b8f048d5381f01c837b5a5b85 && git checkout 1bcbb13d7278e37b8f048d5381f01c837b5a5b85
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f506b79d85790a8f74a762ac4031090c7fbdae25 c22645ebea8b55d8c6e6592c8546d731657720cb && git checkout -B drift-repro f506b79d85790a8f74a762ac4031090c7fbdae25 && git merge --no-ff c22645ebea8b55d8c6e6592c8546d731657720cb

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f506b79d85790a8f74a762ac4031090c7fbdae25
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f506b79d85790a8f74a762ac4031090c7fbdae25` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8b9f159f2d3638304f2a969fad6c395dac5ea200`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-settings-declared.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sign-in-method-floor.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-settings-clear.pin.test.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts (`applyConfigPatch`, constructor, `isClientIpAllowed`, `isAuthGateActive`), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-auth-instance.ts (`emailAndPassword` forwarding), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/audience-posture.ts (`assertAudienceConfig`), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/mfa-required-enrollment-predicate.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/allowed-ip-ranges.pin.test.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.ts (`resetNamespace`). The changeset is the prose face: read sentence by sentence, findings under ②, the ACCEPT names them.

Face: declared narrowing (`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset, both line-initial). Card #30312; seat rulings on the card thread: (1) a key resolving `source: 'default'` after a clear or a namespace reset returns to the deployment-declared value in the same pass; (2) ruling A: the sign-in floor judges a cleared `email_password_enabled` at the declared value, `sign-in-method-floor.ts` added to the surface by the seat. Read against the diff merge-base `f18adce2` → head, and the cited code on the head.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Every `isExplicit` branch is covered.** 33 `isExplicit` keys in `applySettings` on the head (lines 2198–2429 of `auth-plugin.ts`); `AUTH_SETTING_RESTORE` names 33 keys, and the first pin holds the table equal to the shipped auth manifest's specifier keys. Per key the arm matches the piece the explicit branch rides: `emailAndPassword` ×5 (`enabled`, `disableSignUp`, `requireEmailVerification`, `minPasswordLength`, `maxPasswordLength`) as their own refusable pieces; `password_reject_breached` as a `plugins` piece (re-judged by `assertScimAdminCoherence` on the merged block, as a save is); `mfa_required` as its own arm; `session_expiry_days` / `session_refresh_days` as a merged `session` block; 20 plain options on the plain patch (`allowed_ip_ranges` among them); rate-limit pair, Google trio and audience trio as groups. Correct.
2. **The declared value is exactly the boot input.** `captureDeclaredAuthOptions(authConfig)` runs in `init()` after `applyEnvSocialProviderFallbacks`, after `auth:configure`, and immediately before `new AuthManager(authConfig)` (head lines 761, 766, 809–811): the snapshot is the object the manager was constructed from, one level copied. Google restores through `this.configuredSocialProviders`, the same post-`auth:configure` snapshot the explicit branch starts from. Where the deployment declared nothing the restore writes `undefined`, which every consumer read resolves to the same built-in default boot used: `isClientIpAllowed` (`!ranges || ranges.length === 0` → open, so `undefined` equals the `[]` PR #30309 wrote), `isAuthGateActive` (`mfaRequired === true`), `auth-manager-auth-instance.ts` (`enabled: … ?? true`, length fields spread only when `!= null`). Correct.
3. **Env-pinned keys are untouched.** The settings service reports an env override as `source: 'env'`, so `isExplicit` is true and `restoring` is false; `resetNamespace` nulls only `global`/`tenant`/`user` rows. Pinned by the reset-with-`OS_AUTH_LOCKOUT_THRESHOLD` case. Correct.
4. **No clear leaves a refusable piece half-applied.** `mfa_required`: declared on restores as one piece `{ mfaRequired: true, plugins: { twoFactor: true } }` (refused together or applied together); declared off/undefined rides the plain patch and leaves `plugins.twoFactor` standing, which is exactly what an explicit off does. The MFA enrollment predicate reads a `null` as off (`readToggle` → false), so a clear is never refused there; a declared-on deployment under `OS_AUTH_TWO_FACTOR=false` restores to its own boot state, as the acceptance note says. Google trio: restored whole only when none of the three is explicit (`groupRestoring`), else the explicit branch composes from the stored keys as before. Audience: restored whole through one `applyConfigPatch({ audience })` after the `emailAndPassword` pieces, only when `audience_posture` is not stored, by the same merged-result validation; a sibling stored without a posture stays IGNORED. `require_email_verification` restores with `requireEmailVerificationFrom: 'deployment'`, so `assertAudienceConfig` sees the deployment's own declaration, as at boot. A refused restore is pushed to `owed` and so stays in `authSettingsFromStore` for the next pass; the standing value keeps ruling meanwhile, as for a refused save. Correct.
5. **Floor change is confined to the lockout case.** The only changed input is the fallback `readToggle` uses for a cleared `email_password_enabled` in the batch (`deps.declaredEmailPasswordEnabled?.() ?? true`); an env override still wins in `valueAfter`; the Google-key fallbacks are unchanged; the refusal still requires no other way in after the save (`otherSignInMethods`, `googleAfter`). A deployment that declared email and password on, or absent, is judged exactly as before. The floor is registered on `setMany`, which `resetNamespace` also goes through, so a "Restore defaults" that would leave no way in is refused the same way; before the PR the same reset was saved and applied nothing. Within the declared narrowing. Correct.
6. **`allowed_ip_ranges` behaviour unchanged.** PR #30309's two fields are gone; the key rides the plain arm with `restoring` replacing `allowedIpRangesFromSettings`; the restored value is the declared list copied, or `undefined` (open) when undeclared. The three #30203 clear pins in `allowed-ip-ranges.pin.test.ts` are untouched and the dev's ablation A1 reports all three red when the plain arm is removed. Correct.
7. **Declaration.** `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`: the accept set of a published HTTP door (`PUT /api/settings/auth`, `SettingsService.setMany('auth', …)`) narrows by one save; no TypeScript export moves (`sign-in-method-floor.ts` and `auth-settings-declared.ts` are not re-exported from `index.ts`; `auth-plugin.ts` adds imports and private fields only; the new optional `declaredEmailPasswordEnabled?` field sits on an interface outside the package's `exports` map). `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: nothing an author writes changes. `Skills-docs: none — REASON` present as the narrowing arm requires; verified no file under `skills/**` names `email_password_enabled`, `allowed_ip_ranges` or `lockout_threshold`. `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx` names the keys but documents neither the sign-in floor nor this clear, so no documented statement becomes false; its line "Changes take effect immediately; no restart is required" becomes true for clears. Correct.
8. **Session merge** (dev deviation 3): a stored `session_expiry_days` / `session_refresh_days` now overrides its field over the declared `session` block instead of replacing the block. Follows ruling (1): a declared field nobody stored rules. Named in the changeset. Correct.
9. **Residual of ruling (1), pre-existing and declared:** with one rate-limit key cleared while the other stays stored, the explicit branch still composes the pair from the stored key and the built-in `10` / `60`, not from the declared `rateLimit`; unchanged from before the PR, in the PR's Acceptance notes with `carrier: none`. Not a defect this PR introduces; the seat decides whether it is a follow-up card (recommended: a small one, since the card's wanted line reads "every `isExplicit` branch").
10. **Pins are ablation-plausible.** The reported red counts per ablation (A1 7, A2 3, A3 1, A4 1, A5 1, A6 1, A7 2, A8 1, A9 2, A10 1, A11 1) match the cases in the new file that each arm alone can turn red (for example A7's two are the rate-limit pair case and the reset case's `rateLimit` assertion; A9's two are the two audience cases). The refusal pin asserts status `400`, `error.code` `SETTINGS_VALIDATION`, the field error `invalid_value` at `email_password_enabled`, and the running value unchanged; the preservation pin beside it asserts the same clear saves and applies with Google standing.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-auth` (published) takes `patch`: `Metadata-protocol: none`, and a non-protocol narrowing ships `patch` with its BREAKING carriers (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3). Carriers present and well-formed: title `fix(plugin-auth)!:`, body `**BREAKING** accept-set narrowing …`, exactly one `adr-0087:` marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription) …`, which `readDisposition` parses (category, then the why); the body carries an administrator remedy, no consumer code rewrite. `Check Changeset` (which runs `check-adr-0087-registration --base`) is `success` on this head. Both declaration lines and `Skills-docs:` are line-initial in the changeset. Changeset sentences read against the diff: the fix paragraph, the refused-clear paragraph (`constraint.lastSignInMethod: email_password` is what the floor returns) and the session-lifetime paragraph all hold. One wording note for the seat's ACCEPT, not a correction: the refused-clear paragraph speaks of clearing the toggle; "Restore defaults" on the namespace is the same door and is refused in the same lockout state.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev `deviations`: (1) surface widened to `sign-in-method-floor.ts` — the seat's ruling A authorised it; (2) harness assign/review step skipped — per the dispatch order; (3) session merge — judged under ① item 8. `open_questions`: none. `security_findings`: none. `out_of_scope_findings`: one observation, judged under ① item 9.
- Author: PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay); no out-of-relay author to name.
- Check-runs on `8b9f159f` at 2026-11-05T12:00Z: 30 success, 13 skipped (UI and opt-in lanes), 4 `in_progress` (`Test Core` 1–4 of 8), 0 failure. Not green yet; nothing red.
- **Owed before queue (the dispatching seat's gate, not this face):** the full dogfood battery reading is on `f58be8f5`, not on the head. `8b9f159f` is `f58be8f5` plus a merge of `origin/main` that moves `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts` (12 lines, `getPublicConfig().features.emailDelivery`) and `packages/qa/dogfood/test/record-page-timeline.dogfood.test.ts`. The plugin-auth suite and typecheck were re-run on the head and are green per the body; the review checklist pins the `(narrowing)` dogfood reading to the head. The seat either re-runs the battery on the landing head or records why the merge-only delta carries the `f58be8f5` reading forward.

### ④ Design judgment

- **The narrowing against the published surface on `main`.** The published spec declares no capability to clear `auth.email_password_enabled` into a state with no sign-in method; the sign-in floor (PR #30298) already refuses an explicit save into that state. Before this PR a clear passed the floor on the manifest default and then applied nothing, so the state the floor exists to refuse was reachable only on paper. With clears applying, judging the cleared toggle at the declared value makes the floor's own refusal real for the one input it mis-read. It takes no declared capability away at the consumer; it closes a gap between what was saved and what ran. Holds.
- **`auth-settings-declared.ts`** against ruling (1): one table and one snapshot instead of thirty `else` arms; the table is held to the manifest by a pin, so a new manifest key without an arm fails the suite rather than silently keeping its stored value. Restores travel the same piece as saves, so the manager's verdict, not the plugin's, decides a restore. `copyDeclared` is one level deep: `audience.allowedEmailDomains` and `rateLimit.customRules` remain shared between snapshot and running config after a restore; no mutation site reads them in place (`applyConfigPatch` builds new objects, the audience replaces whole), so this is a note, not a defect.
- **`auth-plugin.ts`** against ruling (1): `authSettingsFromStore` keeps "boot restores nothing" (the spy pin) and the restore arms sit after the explicit branches and before the piece application, so a key is restored in the same pass that reads it as `default`. The per-process set is rebuilt from `isExplicit` on every pass plus `owed`, so a restart or a second node reaches the same answer from the store alone.
- **`sign-in-method-floor.ts`** against ruling A: the dep is optional and absent-means-on, so every other caller of the predicate keeps its reading; the change is one fallback argument. Holds.
- Non-blocking shape note: the new pin file copies the `MockHttp` / `boot` rig of `allowed-ip-ranges.pin.test.ts` verbatim (about 90 lines). There is no single shared harness file for the auth settings binding today (each prior card has its own rig), so the shared-harness rule does not bind here; a later card that touches this binding again should lift the rig into one file rather than copy it a third time.

## Contract review — delta

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c22645ebea8b55d8c6e6592c8546d731657720cb`
Local-runs: none
Scope: the delta `8b9f159f` → `c22645eb` only: the merge of `origin/main` at `f506b79d` (29 commits, among them PR #30449 for #30300 at `a93ef3e3`) into this branch, read as it bears on this PR's declared narrowing (a cleared `email_password_enabled` judged at the deployment's declaration) and on #30449's two doors (the SSO-provider delete floor and the `kernel:ready` no-sign-in-method report). Files read on the head: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sign-in-method-floor.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-settings-clear.pin.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sign-in-method-floor.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, .changeset/30312-auth-settings-clear-applies-default.md, .changeset/30300-keep-the-last-identity-provider.md. The full review of record on `8b9f159f` (comment 6657446697) stands for everything outside this delta; nothing below re-opens it.

Shape of the delta. `c22645eb` is a two-parent merge (`8b9f159f`, `f506b79d`). Exactly two files differ from both parents, that is, carry a resolution by hand: `auth-plugin.ts` and `sign-in-method-floor.ts`. Every other file is byte-identical to one parent: `auth-manager.ts`, `sign-in-method-floor.test.ts`, `auth-manager-before-hook.ts`, `register-sso-provider.test.ts`, `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx` and `.changeset/30300-keep-the-last-identity-provider.md` equal `main`'s; `auth-settings-clear.pin.test.ts`, `auth-settings-declared.ts` and `.changeset/30312-auth-settings-clear-applies-default.md` equal the PR's previous head. The new merge-base is `f506b79d`; the PR's own change set against it is the same five paths as before (two added source files, one added test, one added changeset, two modified sources).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Resolution keeps both PRs' semantics.** `sign-in-method-floor.ts` on the head, diffed against `main`, is exactly this PR's 14-line change (the module comment, the optional `declaredEmailPasswordEnabled?(): boolean` on `SignInMethodFloorDeps`, and the one fallback argument in `signInMethodFloorPredicate`), applied on top of #30449's version of the file, which brought `ssoProviderDeleteRefusal`, `probeOtherSsoProviders`, `resolveNoSignInMethodReport` and `reportIfNoSignInMethodAtBoot`. `auth-plugin.ts` on the head, diffed against `main`, is this PR's previous patch line for line (interdiff of the two patches: the only difference is two lines re-indented, the `declaredEmailPasswordEnabled` reader and its comment, moved from the inline deps literal into #30449's shared `signInMethodFloorDeps()` constructor); the registration is #30449's one-liner `registerSignInMethodFloor(settings, this.signInMethodFloorDeps(ctx, this.authManager), ctx.logger)`. `auth-manager.ts` carries no content from this PR and equals `main` (#30449's `setSsoProviderDeleteFloor` present). Correct.
2. **Every reader of the new dep, on the head.** Three occurrences in the tree: the interface field (`sign-in-method-floor.ts` line 140), the one read `deps.declaredEmailPasswordEnabled?.() ?? true` as the `readToggle` fallback inside `signInMethodFloorPredicate` (line 421, reached only when the save batch has own property `email_password_enabled`), and the constructor in `auth-plugin.ts` (line 2081). `ssoProviderDeleteRefusal` (line 525) and `resolveNoSignInMethodReport` (line 561) both open with `const config = deps.publicConfig(); if (config.emailPassword?.enabled !== false) return …` and then call `otherSignInMethods` and the provider probes; none of them, nor `otherSignInMethods`, `googleAfter` or `valueAfter`, names the dep. So the SSO delete path and the boot report cannot reach the fallback: both judge the running `publicConfig`, exactly as on `main`, and their verdicts are unchanged by this PR. The dev's claim (only the save floor's batch reading uses it) is what the code shows. Correct.
3. **The shared constructor is safe at every call site.** The dep is a closure over `this.declaredAuthOptions`, which is declared with initializer `{}` (line 569) and assigned by `captureDeclaredAuthOptions(authConfig)` at line 816, before `new AuthManager(authConfig)` (818) and before the first `signInMethodFloorDeps()` call (824, the delete floor handed to the manager). Read before capture it would resolve `undefined !== false` → on, the same as absent. The other two call sites (`kernel:ready` report at 1552, `bindAuthSettings` registration at 2158) run after init. Nothing in the constructor's other fields moved. Correct.
4. **The cleared-toggle fallback behaves as reviewed.** The predicate's input is unchanged from `8b9f159f`: a clear in the batch reads `readToggle(null, declared)`, env override still wins through `valueAfter`, the Google keys keep their `true` fallbacks, the refusal still needs `otherSignInMethods` empty and `googleAfter` false. The two pins on the head are byte-identical to the reviewed ones: the refusal case (declared `emailAndPassword.enabled: false` plus Google, Setup turns email and password on, then Google off, then clears → `400`, `SETTINGS_VALIDATION`, field `email_password_enabled` with `invalid_value`, running `enabled` still `true` after settle) and the preservation case (same declaration, Google left standing, the clear answers `200` and the running value goes to `false` with Google still defined). #30449's door 1 harness turns email and password off with an explicit `false` in the batch, which `readToggle` reads as the value regardless of fallback, so that harness is not touched by the fallback either. Correct.
5. **No test dropped or weakened.** `auth-settings-clear.pin.test.ts`: 17 `it` cases, identical blob to `8b9f159f`. `sign-in-method-floor.test.ts` (#30449's shared harness, the PR never edits it): identical blob to `main`; it builds its `SignInMethodFloorDeps` literal without the new optional field, which the `?` admits, and both `Type Check · workspace` and `TypeScript Type Check` are green on the head. `register-sso-provider.test.ts` and the floor's `self-hosting.mdx` section equal `main`. #30449's changeset `30300-keep-the-last-identity-provider.md` is present on the head. Correct.
6. **Carriers unchanged and still true on the merged tree.** `.changeset/30312-auth-settings-clear-applies-default.md` is byte-identical to the reviewed one: `'@objectstack/plugin-auth': patch`, title with `!`, line-initial `Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — …`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `Skills-docs: none — …`, exactly one `adr-0087:` HTML-comment marker reading `not-required (no-migration-prescription) …`, and the `**BREAKING** accept-set narrowing …` paragraph. The PR title keeps `fix(plugin-auth)!:`. `Check Changeset` is `success` on `c22645eb`. Correct.
7. **Boot order interaction with #30449's `kernel:ready` block.** #30449 awaits `ensureAuthSettingsBound(ctx)` and then reports; this PR's restore arm restores only keys the running config previously took from the store in this process, and the first pass takes none (the "boot restores nothing" spy pin, ablation A11), so the report reads the same facts as on `main`. Not a change. Correct.
